doc.title: Rudy Van Gelder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: First commercial record with Joe Mooney and the Al Collins radio play
summary: His first commercial record was a trio with Bucky Pizzarelli, Joe Mooney and Bob Carter, and disc jockey Al Collins popularised a track.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Okay, so then what other musicians were… from Lennie Tristano you…?

Well the first commercial record I ever did, that wasn’t, and that was Lennie’s Record. The first one that I ever did, that was with Bucky Pizzarelli, a player by the name of Joe Mooney, and a bass player, believe it or not, by the name Bob Carter; not Ron, Bob Carter. He was very…I made the trio and we took it into New York to be mastered, and that was the first commercial record I ever made. A lot of people still have it, they tell me.
And you were telling me that that radio disc jockey…

There was a radio disc jockey in New York City called Al Collins. Collins on a Cloud was the name of his program, everyday in the afternoon. It was wonderful; it was very cool, nice music. It was a popular program. And one of the songs that Joe Mooney did, it was, “Will Be Together Again.” That got quite popular, everybody loved it, and he used that as the background for talking between the albums, between the records.
So you heard that on the radio?
Did you have a big radio? One of those…
Yes, a console radio at home. A lot of people did. I had little ones too; I always had some kind of radio happening.
